title: PowerRename and File Locksmith context menu entries missing in v0.94.0 and later
author: Gowntn
summary: PowerRename and File Locksmith context-menu entries fail to appear after runtime-registration changes, with a separate ARM64 report describing PowerRename disappearing after the first invocation.
next_action: Reproduce the Windows 10 always-missing case and the ARM64 disappears-after-first-use case as separate test variants.

confidence.rationale: Both variants have useful evidence, but their shared cause is not established.

judgment.rationale: The main Windows 10 report gives a clear version boundary and diagnostic ZIP; the ARM64 comment adds a distinct intermittent re-registration pattern that should be tested separately rather than treated as proven identical.
evidence: The main report says both entries are missing on Windows 10 22H2 from 0.94.0 onward and work on 0.93.0.
Both GitHub and Store installation methods were tested.
The reporter ruled out blocked shell-extension CLSIDs.
An ARM64 commenter reports PowerRename registers once, then later logs enabled without a matching registration-completed line; File Locksmith remains healthy.
Current installer and module code contain runtime package registration/unregistration paths for these context-menu modules.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the Windows 10 always-missing case and the ARM64 disappears-after-first-use case as separate test variants.

fix_assessment.rationale: The issue contains at least two environments and possibly two failure modes; current evidence does not justify one shared code fix.

issue_context.summary: PowerRename and File Locksmith context-menu entries fail to appear after runtime-registration changes, with a separate ARM64 report describing PowerRename disappearing after the first invocation.
known_information: The main reporter attached a 0.100-era diagnostic ZIP.
The ARM64 report includes logs from both 0.93.0 and 0.100.2.
Toggling the module or restarting Explorer temporarily restores PowerRename in the ARM64 case.
inferences: Registration verification or runtime package state may be involved, but the Windows 10 and ARM64 behaviors may not share a root cause.
issue_context.analysis: A two-variant maintainer repro will prevent one environment's diagnosis from being incorrectly generalized to the other.
initial_investigation: Read the full main report and ARM64 diagnostic trail.
Confirmed public source contains runtime registration and cleanup paths for context-menu packages.

actions.label: Reproduce context-menu registration failures
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Compare Windows 10 missing entries with ARM64 one-use disappearance
prerequisites: Windows 11 ARM64 test system if available
setup: Install the current stable release by the same scope used in each report.
Keep Explorer and module logs available.
steps: On Windows 10, right-click files and folders after install and after Explorer restart.
On ARM64, toggle PowerRename, invoke it once, then repeat in a new Explorer session.
Compare package registration state and registration-completed log entries for PowerRename and File Locksmith.
Repeat after sign-out/sign-in without changing module settings.
reproduce.expected_result: Both enabled context-menu commands should remain registered and visible across repeated Explorer sessions.
